bullets.title: DELL: Blowout Quarter — AI Server Guidance Raised to $74B, ISG Margins at 15%
bullets.body: DELL surged ~9% pre-market after a massive beat driven by ISG revenue +89% y/y vs 75% guide and ISG margins of 15% vs ~11-12% estimates. FY27 AI server guidance raised to $74B from $60B, with $95B backlog and 6,500+ customers; conventional server growth guided to 100%+ y/y. GS raised non-GAAP FY28 EPS ~38% to $30.53; Wolfe keeps Peer Perform citing 12.8x CY28 P/E above historical 10x average and memory-pricing margin risk.

bullets.title: MDB: -14% on Earnings Despite Atlas Record; Street Split on Durability
bullets.body: MongoDB fell ~13-14% despite Atlas revenue +28.9% y/y (beat guidance by ~290bps) and record ~$53M net new quarterly ARR. Market concerns center on Atlas growth being flat-to-decelerating vs expectations and 2H sustainability. GS maintains Buy; DA Davidson raises PT to $465 (51x FY28 FCF); Citi raises PT to $565 on 12x FY28 EV/Sales, noting 20%+ total revenue growth overlooked by markets.

bullets.title: UBER: 10% RIF (~3,300 Jobs), $825M Savings Reinvested into AV — Not Demand Weakness
bullets.body: Uber cutting ~10% of workforce (~3,300 employees) with estimated gross annualized savings of $825M+, driven by AI productivity gains (70%+ of pull requests now AI-attributed, agentic WAUs up 7x). Stock up ~1.8% pre-market as savings are to be reinvested in AV and growth initiatives rather than margin expansion. Craig Johnson's technical model adds UBER to buy list on topside breakout.

bullets.title: VRT: Acquires UtilityInnovation Group for $1.45B + $1.15B Earnout to Expand AI Power Architecture
bullets.body: Vertiv acquiring UtilityInnovation Group (UIG) — which has contracts with all five hyperscalers and 227MW in 2026/27 — for $1.45B base cash plus up to $1.15B earnout at 13x FY27E EBITDA. Deal extends VRT upstream into campus power architecture with source-agnostic platform; expected to close 4Q26 with Year 1 EPS accretion. Oppenheimer rates Outperform, noting expanded content/MW and pull-through for existing VRT offerings.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Court Rejects DOJ Ad Tech Divestiture; Berkshire Adds $17B; Gemini 4 Pre-Training Complete
bullets.body: A federal judge denied the DOJ's request to force divestiture of Google's ad tech unit, imposing only behavioral remedies — stock up ~$4 on the news. Separately, Berkshire Hathaway's CEO called GOOGL a 'significant player' in AI and added $17B of shares in Q2, making it Berkshire's third-largest holding. DeepMind's chief confirms Gemini 4 pre-training complete with encouraging early results, and Gemini 3.8 Flash imminent.

bullets.title: CRM: Agentforce Adoption Accelerating; Salesforce Invests in Wonderful's $550M AI OS Round
bullets.body: Truist is incrementally positive on Salesforce after a webinar showing 10,000+ customers with at least one AI product in production (more than doubled since February), with Agentforce Builders expected to more than double to ~1,200 by year-end and premium vertical pricing emerging. Separately, Wonderful closed a $550M Series C at $5B valuation with Salesforce participation, expanding its enterprise AI operating system to 35+ markets.

bullets.title: SNOW: Tonight's Earnings — Street Expects ~35-36% Product Revenue Growth, Guide Raise to 33-34%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley expects SNOW 2Q product revenue of +35-36% (vs. +34% last quarter and +30% consensus) with 3Q guide of ~+34% (vs. +20% consensus); FY27 guide likely raised to +33-34% from current +31%. Citi similarly targets ~36% 2Q growth with 3Q around +32%. SNOW noted as a crowded long at a recent infrastructure roundtable, with pre-market sympathy selling of ~2.4% on the MDB miss.

bullets.title: AVGO: FY27 AI Revenue Focus — Street Expecting $120-150B vs 'Well North of $100B' Guidance
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes the key debate into AVGO's report tonight is whether FY27 AI revenue will be guided to $120-150B vs. the current 'well north of $100B' language. Mizuho includes AVGO among names at risk of de-rating if 2028 AI capex sustainability concerns persist despite strong near-term guidance.

bullets.title: HPE: Tonight's Print — Buyside Expects >$1 EPS vs $0.88-0.93 Guidance; DELL Read-Through Positive
bullets.body: HPE up ~3.8% pre-market on DELL read-through, with buyside expecting Q EPS >$1 vs management guidance of $0.88-0.93c; FY26 EPS buy-side near $3.70 vs current $3.35-3.45 guide. Mizuho flags HPE as a derivative long on DELL strength — 12x P/E, 8x EV/EBITDA, 20% EPS growth potential from AI servers, networking demand, and JNPR synergies.

bullets.title: ORCL: Peak Negative Sentiment; OCI Growth Accelerating with Strong AI Infrastructure Backlog
bullets.body: Zach's AM Attack flags Oracle at peak negative sentiment with OCI growth accelerating and strong backlog expansion. EU antitrust regulators are scrutinizing Oracle's licensing practices (echoing prior SAP case), which represents a headline risk but not a thesis change for bulls.

bullets.title: ADBE: Acquires Indian Market Intelligence Startup Rilo
bullets.body: Adobe acquired Rilo, an Indian-based market intelligence startup, to expand its capabilities. No financial terms disclosed.

bullets.title: NVDA: Phase 2 Semiconductor Tariffs Risk Rising; Data Center Exemption Potentially at Risk
bullets.body: Hedgeye flags >50% probability of broader Phase 2 Section 232 semiconductor tariffs beyond the current 25% on advanced chips, potentially covering servers, PCs, and electronics. Critically, removal of the blanket data center exemption from Phase 1 tariffs is under discussion; Trump-Xi meeting Sept 24 seen as influential with enactment possible in January 2027. This creates margin risk for NVDA-adjacent infrastructure suppliers and could pressure AI capex spending plans.

bullets.title: FSLR: -20% in Past Month — MS Hosting Bull/Bear Debate on Tariff Clarity vs Execution Risk
bullets.body: FSLR has declined nearly 20% over the past month, underperforming broader clean tech by ~8%, ahead of the administration's tariff decision on polysilicon/solar modules. Morgan Stanley hosting a bull/bear webinar Sept 8 — bulls see compelling valuation post-tariff clarity while bears point to execution risk around whether FSLR can realize higher selling prices and re-accelerate bookings.

bullets.title: CRDO: -8.3% Pre-Market on Earnings Despite AEC Dominance; ALAB Sympathy -1.8%
bullets.body: Credo Technology fell ~8.3% pre-market on its earnings print, dragging ALAB down ~1.8% in sympathy. Mizuho remains constructive, citing AEC dominance and new product ramps in optical, silicon photonics, storage interconnect, and ALC cable with SPCX/CSP tailwinds setting up FY28E upside.

bullets.title: DKNG: Wolfe Initiates Outperform as Top Online Gaming Pick
bullets.body: Wolfe Research initiates Gaming & Lodging coverage with DKNG as the top pick in online gaming, citing best-in-class execution and scale in US sports betting returning to growth, with prediction market costs underappreciated by the market. Wolfe is overweight online gaming broadly, seeing multiple paths for sustained growth including potential new state legalizations.

bullets.title: MSFT: G42 AI Startup (Microsoft Shareholder) in Early Discussions to Raise 'Billions'
bullets.body: G42, the Abu Dhabi-based AI startup in which Microsoft holds a stake, is in early-stage discussions with prospective investors to raise billions of dollars. Deal size and details remain undecided. Mizuho separately flags MSFT as a top large-cap long for its software exposure, better FCF, and compelling AI upside via Azure.

bullets.title: TSM / NVDA / MU: Sands Capital Bullish — AI Agents Could Drive 10-20x DRAM Growth
bullets.body: Sands Capital PM argues AI agents at low penetration with rapidly improving capabilities should keep compute and memory supply constrained, potentially driving 10-20x growth in DRAM demand — a structural reset in memory pricing. TSMC is flagged as the 'kingmaker' with pricing power; NVIDIA seen sustaining GPU demand despite algorithm changes; Amazon and Alphabet are preferred hyperscalers.

bullets.title: SEI: Acquires Omega for $308M to Add Heavy Civil/Data Center Construction Capacity
bullets.body: SEI acquiring Omega Foundation Services for ~$308M (3.6M shares + $101M cash + $28M debt assumption), adding heavy civil and data center construction capabilities with immediate EPS and FCF/share accretion expected. SEI has ~800 MW uncontracted and management signals further business expansions are coming.

bullets.title: ESTC: Pictet Reduces Stake to 4.99% from 5.2% via 13D/A; Remains Active on Governance
bullets.body: Pictet Asset Management filed a 13D/A reducing its Elastic stake from 5.2% to 4.99%, crossing below the 5% disclosure threshold. The holder notes continued active engagement with the company on business practice and governance initiatives.

bullets.title: APP Removed from Craig Johnson Technical Model on Long-Term Uptrend Violation
bullets.body: Craig Johnson's technical model deleted APP from the portfolio after it violated long-term uptrend support. ROKU was also removed as profits were taken. UBER was simultaneously added on a topside breakout with multi-month highs.
